field_candidates.value: At least 8-C, likely High 8-C physically, possibly far higher, with at least 9-A energy beams, possibly far higher Name: Michael Jon Carter, or "Booster Gold" Origin: The DC Animated Universe Gender: Male Age: Appears to be in his 20s Classification: Human, Member of the Justice League

*Superhuman Physical Characteristics (See Attack Potency, Lifting Strength, and Durability) *Flight *Energy Projection (Can fire energy blasts and beams) *With Skeets, Booster has access to Genius Intelligence, Information Analysis (Scanned a woman for life signs) and Air Manipulation (Blew smoke away with a fan)

At least Building Level, likely Large Building Level physically (Fought a sentient building, shifting it backward with his punches - later holding himself in place against the pull of a gravitational anomaly that sucked a building in even whilst closer to said anomaly than the building was. Defeated a building-sized robot, albeit offscreen. Effortlessly knocked doors off their hinges), possibly far higher (Managed to hold himself back from getting totally sucked in by the "mini black hole" after its pull had become powerful enough to seemingly bend several buildings), with at least Small Building Level energy beams (Destroyed the awning over a subway station and blasted away the resulting rubble. Damaged the exterior of a rock formation), possibly far higher (Possibly equal to or greater than the power of his physical strength) - Booster would not gain black hole strength scaling from holding back the gravitational anomaly, as clearly it isn't as powerful as a normal black hole (it is stated to be uncontrolled, yet it does not instantly swallow the planet, which an IRL black hole the size of a quarter would), and therefore he wouldn't scale to IRL Black Holes.

At least Superhuman (Dodged a speeding train at close range), with Superhuman flight speed (Traversed a city pretty quickly)- Booster would not gain black hole speed scaling from reacting to being sucked in by the gravitational anomaly, as clearly it isn't as powerful as a normal black hole (it is stated to be uncontrolled, yet it does not instantly swallow the planet, which an IRL black hole the size of a quarter would), and therefore he wouldn't scale to IRL Black Holes. Even normal humans are shown reacting to being sucked in by the anomaly, meaning clearly it isn't a real black hole which sucks things up faster than light.

At least Building Class, likely Large Building Class, possibly far higher (Should scale to his physical power as per Newton's Third Law. Survived attacks from a sentient building. Shrugged off being hit by a train and having a car fall on him) - Booster would not gain black hole durability scaling from holding back the gravitational anomaly, as clearly it isn't as powerful as a normal black hole (it is stated to be uncontrolled, yet it does not instantly swallow the planet, which an IRL black hole the size of a quarter would), and therefore he wouldn't scale to IRL Black Holes.

Normal Human Weaknesses. Lacks actual confidence in himself, only putting up a facade of overconfidence. Note: Bruce Timm has stated that the original DCAU tie-in comics are not canon, with the only tie in comics that have statements to the contrary (other than Batman: The Adventures Continue, which has so many continuity issues that it's essentially impossible to argue it's canon) being Justice League Infinity, the Batman and Harley Quinn tie in comics, and specifically the first annual of Batman Adventures. Ergo, I only consider those three comics canon. Category:Goulden1998 Category:Tier 8 Category:Tier 9
